2609.24625.title: Custom Named Entity Recognition and Topic Classification for Global Health Publications
2609.24625.paper_summary: How should natural language processing models be selected and adapted for global health literature in environments where annotated data and computational resources are limited? This thesis investigates these challenges through experiments on semantic tag discovery, named entity recognition (NER), and multi-label topic classification. First, skip-gram word2vec models trained on progressively larger specialized corpora are compared with BioWordVec to assess how corpus size and domain context influence tag discovery. Vocabulary coverage and qualitative evaluation indicate that broader coverage does not necessarily yield more useful domain-specific associations. The analysis then turns to entity extraction, comparing convolutional spaCy models with a RoBERTa-based transformer on 1,000 annotated sentences. Under a lenient scoring protocol, the transformer achieves 0.80 micro-F1 versus 0.65-0.69 for convolutional models, but takes 82 seconds rather than 5-6 seconds. This trade-off motivates fine-tuning convolutional models and integrating a disease recognizer that achieves 81.33% test F1 on the NCBI Disease Corpus. Combined with PDF preprocessing, entity filtering, and MeSH enrichment, the resulting pipeline supports document-level indexing. To complement entity extraction with thematic annotation, MiniLM-based few-shot classification is compared with BART-MNLI zero-shot inference across 50 topics and 1,000 handcrafted test sentences. BART-MNLI achieves 95.2% single-label accuracy versus 59%; reported multi-label accuracies are 88% and 32% under partly manual assessment. However, its higher inference cost limits practical integration. The results show where domain specialization and lightweight adaptation offer practical value, and where transformer accuracy justifies higher inference costs, providing an empirical basis for building knowledge systems under resource constraints.
2609.24625.paper_summary_zh: 如何在標註數據和計算資源有限的環境中選擇和調整自然語言處理模型，以應對全球健康文獻？本論文通過對語義標籤發現、命名實體識別（NER）和多標籤主題分類的實驗來探討這些挑戰。首先，對逐步增大專門語料庫訓練的skip-gram word2vec模型與BioWordVec進行比較，以評估語料庫大小和領域上下文如何影響標籤發現。詞彙覆蓋率和質量評估表明，較廣的覆蓋並不一定會產生更有用的領域特定關聯。分析隨後轉向實體提取，將卷積spaCy模型與基於RoBERTa的Transformer在1,000個標註句子上進行比較。在寬鬆的評分協議下，Transformer達到0.80的微F1，而卷積模型則為0.65-0.69，但所需時間為82秒，而不是5-6秒。這種權衡促使對卷積模型進行微調，並整合一個在NCBI疾病語料庫上達到81.33%測試F1的疾病識別器。結合PDF預處理、實體過濾和MeSH豐富，最終的管道支持文檔級索引。為了用主題註釋補充實體提取，基於MiniLM的少量樣本分類與BART-MNLI零樣本推斷在50個主題和1,000個手工製作的測試句子上進行比較。BART-MNLI在單標籤準確率上達到95.2%，而基於MiniLM的準確率為59%；報告的多標籤準確率在部分手動評估下為88%和32%。然而，其較高的推斷成本限制了實際整合。結果顯示了領域專業化和輕量級調整在何處提供實際價值，以及Transformer準確性在何處證明了較高推斷成本的合理性，為在資源限制下構建知識系統提供了實證基礎。
